findings.declaration: normFreeEltOf / normFreeElt (and the two ad-hoc unfoldings in comp_phi_normFreeEltOf and F8_skeleton.token)
findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def normFreeEltOf (S : Finset ℕ) : ModularCurve.HeckeAlgOne :=
  MvPolynomial.C (S.card : ℤ) - ∑ d ∈ S, ModularCurve.diamondGen d
findings.problem: The definitions have no action lemma, and no `normFreeElt M p = normFreeEltOf (normFreeRepsAt M p)` unfolding lemma. Every consumer that needs `normFreeEltOf S • a` unfolds the definition inside `simp only [normFreeEltOf, sub_smul, Finset.sum_smul, heckeModuleOneBar_C_smul]` (line 477). `F8_skeleton.token` repeats it as `rw [normFreeElt, normFreeEltOf, sub_smul, Finset.sum_smul, heckeModuleOneBar_C_smul, ...]` (line 2372). The same four-step expansion is therefore duplicated, and callers must pass the raw definition names to simp or rw. The result is that `normFreeElt (M * p) p • a` can only be handled by unfolding the definition, so the normal form depends on which proof expands it.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma next to the definitions, for example `normFreeEltOf_smul (N) (S) (a : JOne N) : (letI := ModularCurve.heckeModuleOneBar N; normFreeEltOf S • a) = (S.card : ℤ) • a - ∑ d ∈ S, ModularCurve.diamondGen d • a`. Add `normFreeElt_def : normFreeElt M p = normFreeEltOf (ModularCurve.normFreeRepsAt M p) := rfl`. Use the first lemma for `hlin` and for the first step of `token`. Consider making it `@[simp]`, since the right-hand side is built only from existing simp-normal pieces (`zsmul`, `Finset.sum`, `diamondGen •`) and the left-hand side's head `normFreeEltOf` is not a simp unfolding target.
findings.benefit: Callers stop unfolding the definition, and the two duplicated rewrite chains collapse into one lemma. Later steps (`heckeModuleOneBar_diamondGen_smul`, `normFreeEnd_apply`, which is already simp) can then be applied from one canonical form.

findings.excerpt:
theorem castPt_castPt {B T X : Scheme.{0}} {t t' : T ⟶ B} {f : X ⟶ B} (h : t = t') (x : SchemeHomOver t f) :
    castPt h.symm (castPt h x) = x := Subtype.ext rfl
findings.problem: Only the projection lemma `castPt_coe` is tagged `@[scoped simp]`. The lemmas that eliminate or push through casts are plain theorems: `castPt_castPt` (cancels a round trip), `castPt_mul` and `castPt_comp` (move the cast outward). They are consumed only by hand-written `rw`. In `eqv`, `left_inv` is closed by `simp only [...]` followed by `exact Subtype.ext rfl`, and `right_inv` needs `show ... ; rw [castPt_castPt, ...]`. `eqv_symm_comp` also uses `show ... ; rw [..., castPt_comp]`. The simp interface is therefore half-populated: simp can see through `.1` of a cast but cannot cancel a cast or commute it with `mul` or `comp`.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `castPt_castPt` with `@[scoped simp]`; its left-hand side is a strictly smaller term, so there is no cycle. Also tag `castPt_comp` and `castPt_mul`, oriented as they are (cast pulled outward to a single outermost `castPt`). Add the matching `castPt_castPt'` for the `h` and `h.symm` order, or a `castPt_rfl : castPt rfl x = x` lemma. Then `left_inv` and `right_inv` can be `simp`-closed.
findings.benefit: The cast-transport proofs in `exists_abelianSubvariety_genericFibre_of_endomorphisms` (`left_inv`, `right_inv`, `map_mul'`, `eqv_symm_comp`) lose their `show` and `rw` boilerplate. The `castPt` cluster then has a normal form (at most one outermost `castPt`) that works in the same way as the already-simp `castPt_coe`.

findings.declaration: F8c_nsmul_val / F8c_schemeHomOverComp_idPoint vs. hschemeNsmul in F8_skeleton
findings.excerpt:
theorem F8c_nsmul_val {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) (n : ℕ)
    (x : SchemeHomOver t f) :
    (L.nsmul t n x).1 = x.1 ≫ L.schemeNsmul n := by
findings.problem: `(L.nsmul t n x).1 = x.1 ≫ L.schemeNsmul n` is the canonical rewrite that turns `nsmul` on points into composition with the scheme-level multiplication-by-n map. It is buried in a section as an untagged, `F8c_`-prefixed lemma, and it is not stated next to `schemeNsmul`. `F8_skeleton` therefore re-derives the same fact inline as `hschemeNsmul` (lines 2424–2431), including a private copy of `F8c_schemeHomOverComp_idPoint` (`hw := Subtype.ext (Category.comp_id _)`). The simp interface for `schemeNsmul` and `nsmul` is missing, so downstream code cannot reach the composition normal form. Instead, `rw [hschemeNsmul ..., hgpow, ← hz, ← hιpow]` is hand-orchestrated (line 2472).
findings.proposed_change: Move `F8c_schemeHomOverComp_idPoint` and `F8c_nsmul_val` into the RelativeGroupLaw API (Definitions/Def_GoodReductionJacobian_RelativeGroupLawKernel.lean, next to `schemeNsmul`). Drop the `F8c_` prefix, tag `F8c_nsmul_val` `@[simp]` (it is a coe-projection lemma with a strictly different head, `schemeNsmul` is not simp, so there is no loop), and drop the `u`-universe restriction. Replace `hschemeNsmul` by `(RelativeGroupLaw.nsmul_val LN _ n w).symm`.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated proof and gives users one oriented lemma for `(nsmul ...).1`, so the composition normal form becomes available to simp. It also avoids the private `hw` copy in the 2400-line `F8_skeleton`.
